review_notes:
I read all of Primary.lean (lines 1–167). I also grepped Mathlib for existing helpers. Mathlib has `Ideal.IsPrimary.comap` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/IsPrimary.lean:76) and `Ideal.comap_bot_of_injective` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean:463). It has no lemma that transports `⊥.IsPrimary` along an injective ring hom.

The main repeated pattern is `simpa only [Ideal.comap_bot_of_injective f hf] using h.comap f`. It appears three times in `isPrimary_bot_mvPolynomial_of_finite`, for the rename, empty and option cases. A similar 3-line `ne_top` block, `congrArg (Ideal.comap C) htop` followed by `simpa` with `comap_bot_of_injective` and `comap_top`, appears in both `isPrimary_bot_polynomial` and `isPrimary_bot_mvPolynomial`.

I judged this to be short routine API rewriting. A helper `(⊥ : Ideal B).IsPrimary → (⊥ : Ideal A).IsPrimary` for injective `f : A →+* B` would be a thin wrapper around `IsPrimary.comap` plus one rewrite. It would save only a few lines. The `ne_top` blocks go in the opposite direction, and they also differ in the ring and the injectivity lemma used.

The other candidates are not duplicated reasoning. The McCoy/nilpotent argument occurs only in `isPrimary_bot_polynomial`. The finite-variable reduction occurs only in `isPrimary_bot_mvPolynomial`. The quotient argument for `hquot` occurs only in the main theorem. None of these meets the rubric's bar for nontrivial repeated proof machinery. I could not compile any proposed refactor, so I made no claim that one would work.
